--- title: Exit Break --- ## Features - Exit from nested block structures (like code blocks, tables, columns) using keyboard shortcuts. - Leaves only the nearest structure, so Mod+Enter in a code block, callout, image or divider inside a column inserts the new block in that column. - Inserts the block the surrounding container declares as its default, such as a paragraph in a column. ## Kit usage ### Installation The fastest way to add exit break functionality is with the `ExitBreakKit`, which includes pre-configured `ExitBreakPlugin` with keyboard shortcuts. ### Add kit ```tsx import { createEditor } from 'platejs/react'; import { ExitBreakKit } from '@/components/editor/exit-break'; const editor = createEditor({ plugins: [ // ...otherPlugins, ...ExitBreakKit, ], }); ``` ## Manual usage ### Add plugin ```tsx import { ExitBreakPlugin } from 'platejs'; import { createEditor } from 'platejs/react'; const editor = createEditor({ plugins: [ // ...otherPlugins, ExitBreakPlugin, ], }); ``` ### Configure plugin ```tsx import { ExitBreakPlugin } from 'platejs'; import { createEditor } from 'platejs/react'; const editor = createEditor({ plugins: [ // ...otherPlugins, ExitBreakPlugin.configure({ shortcuts: { insert: { keys: 'mod+enter' }, insertBefore: { keys: 'mod+shift+enter' }, }, }), ], }); ``` - `shortcuts.insert`: Defines a keyboard [shortcut](/docs/plate/plugin-shortcuts) to exit and insert block after. - `shortcuts.insertBefore`: Defines a keyboard [shortcut](/docs/plate/plugin-shortcuts) to exit and insert block before. ## Keyboard shortcuts Exit the current block structure and insert a new block after. Exit the current block structure and insert a new block before. ## Plugins ### `ExitBreakPlugin` Provides shortcuts that leave the current block structure through [`tx.break.exit`](/docs/plate/api/editor-transforms#txbreakexitoptions). Keyboard shortcuts configuration. Shortcut to exit and insert block after. - **Example:** `{ keys: 'mod+enter' }` Shortcut to exit and insert block before. - **Example:** `{ keys: 'mod+shift+enter' }` ## How exit break works Exit break leaves the nearest structure around the caret. A code block, callout, image or divider is a structure of its own, so exit inserts the new block right after it, inside the same container. From any other block, exit leaves the nearest container that can take a paragraph beside it: a paragraph in a quote leaves the quote, and a paragraph in a column leaves the whole column group, because the group holds only columns. The new block is the default that the structure's parent declares. ### Exit point determination When you trigger exit break: 1. Starts from the block that holds the caret 2. Stops at that block when it owns its exit: a void such as a divider, an object such as an image, or a text block that declares `ownsExit`, such as a code block or a callout 3. Otherwise walks up its ancestors and stops at the first one that sits directly in the document, or whose parent can hold a text block such as a paragraph 4. Inserts that parent's default block next to the exit point and moves the caret into it Exit passes over a block that owns its exit, and leaves the container instead, when its parent cannot put a plain text block beside it. That happens when the parent has no room or no default block, or when its default needs a property nothing supplies, holds no text, or owns its exit too. Below the top level, the walk also passes a container whose default would put the caret back into a container of the same type. Once exit stops at a container, it never climbs further. When that container's parent declares no default block, has no room for another one, or has a default that needs a property nothing supplies or holds no text, nothing changes. ### Examples **Code Block:** ```tsx // ← Exit point (top-level block) code| // ← Starting position | // ← New paragraph inserted here ``` **Code Block in Column (stays in the column):** ```tsx // ← Exit point (owns its exit) code| // ← Starting position | // ← New paragraph inserted here ``` **Image or Divider in Column:** ```tsx caption| // ← Exit point and starting position | // ← New paragraph inserted here ``` **Paragraph in Column (leaves the column group):** ```tsx // ← Exit point (top-level block) // group allows columns only content| // ← Starting position | // ← New paragraph inserted here ``` **Table in Column (exits at table level):** ```tsx // First exit // ← Exit point (column allows blocks) // table allows rows only // row allows cells only content|// ← Starting position
| // ← New paragraph inserted here // Second exit // ← Exit point (top-level block) // group allows columns only content
| // ← Starting position | // ← New paragraph inserted here ``` ### Custom plugin configuration Declare each custom element's allowed child content and its default. An exit passes ancestors whose parent cannot hold a paragraph, such as a cell in a row, and inserts the default that the landing parent declares: ```tsx import { definePlugin, schema } from 'platejs'; // Table structure const CustomTablePlugin = definePlugin('table', { schema: { element: { content: schema.content.type('tr', { min: 1 }), }, }, }); const CustomTableRowPlugin = definePlugin('tr', { schema: { element: { content: schema.content.types(['td', 'th'], { default: { type: 'td' }, min: 1, }), }, }, }); const CustomTableCellPlugin = definePlugin('td', { schema: { element: { content: schema.content.group('block', { default: { type: 'paragraph' }, min: 1, }), }, }, }); ``` A text block that exit should leave before its container, such as a custom code-like block or a callout whose Enter rule exits, declares `ownsExit`. Without it, the block behaves like a paragraph and exit leaves its container: ```tsx import { definePlugin, schema } from 'platejs'; const NoticePlugin = definePlugin('notice', { rules: { break: { emptyLineEnd: 'deleteExit' } }, schema: { element: schema.element.textBlock({ ownsExit: true }), }, }); ``` Only a text block can declare `ownsExit`. Voids and objects always own their exit.
